spec_match.rationale: Builds and injects a genuine <script type=speculationrules> block (list source, prefetch/prerender, all four eagerness levels, rule tag), feature-detects the injection half with HTMLScriptElement.supports('speculationrules'), and reads back via the real getSpeculations().navigations mapping type/url/tags/eagerness.

interactive.rationale: Four builder fields, inject/read/remove buttons, a generated-ruleset pane, and a navigations report whose source (live read vs derived-from-your-inputs reference) is explicitly disclosed.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises building a live ruleset, picking type/eagerness/tags, injecting it, and seeing those choices surface in the navigations array; all delivered, with the read half honestly gated.

edge_cases.rationale: Separates the two support surfaces (rules injection vs measurement read), handles read-before-inject, empty tag, method-absent, and a throwing call; removal genuinely deletes the injected script element.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5118840377835520 plus the three sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The suite's returns-speculationdata-shape and instance-method assertions back this page's read half; the failures in Chromium 141 are only the expected absent experimental method — notably the injection half genuinely works here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): DOM shows 'Speculation Rules supported ✓' correctly detected in this build with the builder rendered; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; inject/read/remove clicks and a real prefetch observation could not be driven non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the support probe, successful injection with type/eagerness, live reads with counts, and fallback reads.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours and correct button/field styling, but the default-visible support line renders --accent-emerald bold text on --bg-ivory at 0.74rem (~4.0:1), marginally under the WCAG AA 4.5:1 bar for text that size.

accessibility.rationale: Every builder field has a visible label and focus-visible outline, output panes are aria-live, and support/source states are conveyed in words rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (the auto-fit builder grid collapses to one column); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Raise the support-line emerald text to AA contrast
openQuestions.detail: The 'Speculation Rules supported ✓' line — the default state in every current Chrome — is --accent-emerald bold at 0.74rem on ivory, ~4.0:1 versus the 4.5:1 AA requirement. Same emerald-on-light pattern as the sibling pages; a darker emerald token fixes it corpus-wide.

openQuestions.title: Verify an injected rule appears in navigations on a flagged build
openQuestions.detail: The full loop — inject a prefetch rule with a tag, then see {type, url, tags, eagerness} in the live navigations array — needs SpeculationMeasurement enabled, which this Chromium 141 lacks. Run it once flagged and confirm the read matches the derived reference the fallback shows, including whether the injected same-origin URL actually got prefetched (DevTools network) at the chosen eagerness.

summary: A genuinely two-sided lab: the speculation-rules injection half runs for real in today's Chrome (correctly detected in this session) while the measurement read half degrades honestly to a labelled derived reference. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): support probe true, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either class. Open items: the marginal emerald support-line contrast and a flagged-build end-to-end read.
